brief_item.title: ROS2：将DAOS客户端卸载到BlueField-3的RDMA优先对象存储
brief_item.core_conclusion: AI训练与推理的细粒度I/O使主机介导的TCP存储路径成为瓶颈。ROS2将DAOS客户端卸载到NVIDIA BlueField-3 SmartNIC，分离轻量gRPC控制面与UCX/libfabric RDMA数据面，移除数据路径中的主机介导，RDMA模式下端到端性能与主机部署相当。
brief_item.mechanism: DAOS客户端运行于BlueField-3，存储服务端DAOS I/O引擎保持不变；gRPC控制面交换命名空间与能力，高通量数据面走RDMA或TCP（UCX/libfabric），数据不再经过主机CPU，并支持DPU侧多租户隔离与加解密。
brief_item.result: 服务器级CPU上RDMA在大块顺序与小粒度随机I/O均持续优于TCP；RDMA模式下BlueField-3端到端性能与主机相当；SmartNIC上TCP落后于主机。证据来自arXiv摘要，未披露具体吞吐或IOPS数值。
brief_item.boundary: 仅摘要级证据，无绝对吞吐与时延数据；GPU-direct放置为未来工作；评测使用FIO/DFS的本地与远程配置，正文未抓取。
brief_item.project_relevance: [判断]直接契合DPU/SmartNIC随路卸载方向：控制面与数据面分离、RDMA数据面复用的模式可迁移到KVCache跨节点传输与推理网络I/O场景。

facts.title: An RDMA-First Object Storage System with SmartNIC Offload (ROS2)
facts.event_hint: A DPU/SmartNIC-offloaded, RDMA-first object storage design (ROS2) that moves the DAOS client onto an NVIDIA BlueField-3, removing host mediation from the data path for GPU-centric AI training/inference I/O.
facts.problem: AI training and inference impose sustained, fine-grain I/O that stresses host-mediated, TCP-based storage paths, creating a host-CPU bottleneck and limiting data delivery to GPU-centric pipelines.
facts.mechanism: RDMA-first object storage: offloads the DAOS client to an NVIDIA BlueField-3 SmartNIC (DPU); separates a lightweight gRPC control plane (namespace + capability exchange) from a high-throughput RDMA/TCP data plane (UCX/libfabric); removes host mediation from the data path entirely, enabling DPU-resident multi-tenant isolation and inline services (e.g., encryption/decryption).

evidence.claim: On server-grade CPUs, RDMA consistently outperforms TCP for both large sequential and small random I/O.
When the RDMA-driven DAOS client is offloaded to BlueField-3, end-to-end performance is comparable to the host.
TCP on the SmartNIC lags host performance, underscoring the importance of RDMA for offloaded deployments.
SmartNIC offload preserves RDMA efficiency while enabling DPU-resident features such as multi-tenant isolation and inline encryption/decryption.

facts.evaluation_context: Evaluated with FIO/DFS across local and remote configurations on server-grade CPUs and NVIDIA BlueField-3. Abstract reports relative comparisons only; no absolute throughput or latency numbers.
facts.limitations: Abstract-level evidence only; no specific throughput/latency numbers, model sizes, or GPU-direct results in the abstract. GPU-direct placement for LLM tasks is explicitly future work. Full paper body not fetched.
facts.project_relevance: Core fit for the DPU/SmartNIC-offload briefing track: demonstrates that a SmartNIC-offloaded, RDMA-first data plane can match host performance while moving isolation and inline crypto onto the DPU. Relevant pattern transfer to KVCache cross-node transfer (RDMA-first data plane separated from control plane) and to TPN inference-network I/O where host mediation is the bottleneck.

primary source is arXiv 2509.13997 (ROS2, HP Labs authors incl. Dejan Milojicic)
abstract gives qualitative/relative results; absolute throughput/latency figures pending full-text validation

facts.title: An RDMA-First Object Storage System with SmartNIC Offload (ROS2)
facts.event_hint: Proposes ROS2, an RDMA-first object storage design that offloads the DAOS client onto an NVIDIA BlueField-3 SmartNIC to remove host mediation from the AI I/O data path.
facts.problem: AI training and inference impose sustained, fine-grain I/O that stresses host-mediated, TCP-based storage paths; host mediation in the data path becomes a bottleneck for GPU-centric pipelines.
facts.mechanism: ROS2 offloads the DAOS client to an NVIDIA BlueField-3 SmartNIC while leaving the DAOS I/O engine unchanged on the storage server. It splits a lightweight gRPC control plane (namespace and capability exchange) from a high-throughput UCX/libfabric data plane (RDMA or TCP), removing host mediation from the data path.

evidence.claim: On server-grade CPUs, RDMA consistently outperforms TCP for both large sequential and small random I/O.
evidence.condition: FIO/DFS across local and remote configurations on server-grade CPUs

evidence.claim: When the DAOS client runs on BlueField-3, end-to-end performance is comparable to running it on the host, preserving RDMA efficiency after offload.
evidence.baseline: DAOS client on the host CPU
evidence.condition: DAOS client offloaded to NVIDIA BlueField-3 SmartNIC over RDMA

evidence.claim: TCP on the SmartNIC lags host performance, underscoring the importance of RDMA for offloaded deployments.
evidence.condition: DAOS client on BlueField-3 over TCP

facts.evaluation_context: Evaluated with FIO/DFS across local and remote configurations, comparing RDMA vs. TCP data planes and DAOS-client-on-host vs. DAOS-client-on-BlueField-3. Storage server keeps the DAOS I/O engine unchanged.
facts.limitations: Abstract-level only; full body not fetched. The abstract reports qualitative ordering (RDMA > TCP; SmartNIC-RDMA comparable to host; SmartNIC-TCP below host) but no specific throughput/IOPS numbers or magnitudes; exact figures require the full PDF.
facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to DPU/SmartNIC offload: it demonstrates offloading a real object-storage client (DAOS) to BlueField-3 while keeping RDMA line-rate benefit, a concrete pattern for removing host mediation from AI-training/inference storage I/O. The control-plane/data-plane split and UCX/libfabric RDMA datapath align with SmartNIC-offload architecture interests.
